modalLead: Network tests on every bookmark — TCP, Ping, DNS, TLS, HTTP detail and JSON, once or on a schedule — with the checks on your rows, in the bell and on the status page, and a larger weather in the header.

items.text: Test your services from nextDash. The new Tests tab of a bookmark checks a port, a ping, DNS records, a certificate, an HTTP answer or a value in a JSON answer. Run one test right now, or schedule it with a history and alerts.
items.title: Test your services from nextDash

media.alt: The Tests tab of a bookmark: three tiles for its checks, and a Ping check opened with its uptime strip and last result

items.text: Checks show up where you work. A check is a chip beside the tags of its row, a row in the bell when it fails, a new Network tests widget and a line on the status page. A filter in the Bookmarks view lists the bookmarks that have one.
items.title: Checks show up where you work

media.alt: The Bookmarks view filtered on Has checks: four rows, each with its check as a chip beside the tags, and the Check type filter in the rail

items.text: A change in DNS tells you. When the records of a name change, the bell says so, and Accept makes the new answer the one to compare with.
Ping in Docker. Where the container cannot send a ping, the check connects over TCP and says so; the Checks panel shows the one line that allows a real ping.
Five tools for MCP clients. Run a test, list, read, add or delete checks from an MCP client. Off until you switch on Network tests.
The weather, bigger in the header. Beside the clock rule the weather shows an icon and the temperature in large type, with the day and place in two small lines.
items.title: A bigger weather in the header

media.alt: The header with the clock, the greeting, and the weather in large type beside the rule, with the day and place in two small lines

items.text: A new container’s notice is a row in the bell. Undo, Move and Done wait there instead of a card in the corner.
No bell on a phone. The notification bell is hidden on a small screen.
The side panel follows the theme. The tabs of a bookmark’s side panel no longer show black blocks on a see-through look.
